hook: Sprayed MXene films as thin as about 22 nanometers make flexible colors that also hide heat signatures.
summary: The researchers spray stacked Ti3C2Tx sheets into ultrathin films whose thickness sets the color, from yellow to gray at roughly 22 to 154 nanometers. The films also emit little infrared up to 300 degrees C, so they can camouflage in both visible and infrared, and meter-scale sheets were cut and sewn into cloaks. Tests were lab demonstrations, not field camouflage trials.
title: Arbitrarily cuttable and ultrathin MXene structural colors for customizable and wearable multispectral information management.
